records.mine: Willow Creek Mine / Plateau Mining Corporation (Cyprus Plateau — RAG American Coal)
records.equipment: Sección de longwall D-3 (gob detrás de shields)
records.bias_families: B, E, G, I, L, M
records.best_practice: Provide adequate ventilation of the gob behind longwall shields — this is where methane accumulates unseen. Test for methane at the required frequency (every 20 minutes where coal is being mined). Eliminate hydrocarbons from the longwall face: diesel-like vapors turn a contained methane flash into a chain of explosions. Treat a prior methane ignition at the same mine as evidence of a structural problem, not an isolated incident.

records.equipment: Estación de carga de baterías (roof fall) + float coal dust
records.best_practice: After any ignition or explosion, evacuate the entire mine immediately — the atmosphere remains explosive and a second, larger explosion is a recognized pattern. Never allow untrained, unequipped miners to re-enter to rescue injured coworkers; rescue must be performed by equipped mine rescue teams after atmospheric verification. Control float coal dust accumulations and maintain incombustible content so that a methane ignition cannot propagate. Maintain adequate roof support at battery charging stations.

records.mine: No. 4 Mine / Mackie J Coal Company, Inc. (arrendada a Jewell Smokeless Coal Corporation)
records.equipment: Section power center Line Power 600 PC (alta tensión 12,470 VAC)
records.best_practice: Lock out, tag out AND ground every high-voltage circuit before working on it — grounding is the only protection that works if someone energizes the circuit by mistake. Never rely on another person to deenergize the circuit and verify the phases; the person doing the work must verify and lock out personally. Do not allow unqualified persons to perform electrical work without the direct supervision of a qualified person. Test substation protective devices mechanically as well as electrically: a trip circuit that sounds correct may not actually open the breaker. Verify the mine communication system regularly.

records.best_practice: Recognize the hazards associated with changes in strata through transitional geological zones — the slope profile identifies them in advance and they are visible from inside the excavation. Support ribs in those zones with wire mesh securely attached to the roof bolts, or with steel arches and lagging, in addition to conventional bolting. Control water accumulation: strata susceptible to moisture degradation loses strength as it wets. Extend rib support along the full transitional interval, not only at the face.

records.best_practice: Depressurize only one mobile roof support at a time and move them in pairs, offset no more than one-half the length of the companion unit. Ensure every person is in the clear before raising or lowering any MRS on the active pillar line. Never tram mobile roof supports manually. Treat parallel cracks in the roof as a stop-work condition: they reduce stability precisely where support is being removed.

records.best_practice: MSHA Fatal Alert FAB03C13: (1) Never use a 480V AC circuit as a blasting machine — use only MSHA-approved permissible blasting equipment. (2) Only certified shot firers may load, prime, and fire explosives in underground coal mines. (3) Never fire more than 20 shots in one round without a special blasting permit. (4) Immediately report all accidents to MSHA — failure to notify is a separate federal violation. (5) Do not alter the accident scene before MSHA investigation is complete.

records.mine: Sago Mine / Wolf Run Mining Company (Hunter Ridge / ICG)
records.equipment: Sellos de zona abandonada (2 North Mains)
records.best_practice: Build seals to withstand the explosive forces that can develop behind them — the MINER Act raised the standard to 50 psi and later 120 psi as a direct result of Sago. Monitor the atmosphere behind seals for methane accumulation. Store additional SCSRs along all escapeways and verify their functionality. Provide post-accident wireless communication and tracking systems. Ensure mine rescue teams can reach the mine within one hour.

records.mine: Aracoma Alma Mine No. 1 / Aracoma Coal Company (Massey Energy)
records.best_practice: Maintain all stoppings and ventilation controls that separate belt entries from designated escapeways — a single missing stopping can fill the escapeway with smoke. Install and maintain fire detection and suppression systems on all belt conveyors. Install directional lifelines along every escapeway so miners can navigate in zero visibility. During evacuation in dense smoke, maintain continuous physical contact with the crew and never separate from the group.

records.mine: Darby Mine No. 1 / Kentucky Darby LLC
records.equipment: Torch oxígeno-acetileno + sello con fuga de metano
records.best_practice: Before any flame cutting or welding near a seal, test for methane in every area that could be affected — including inside the sealed area itself. A low reading in the entry tells you nothing about the atmosphere behind the seal. Build and verify seals to federal specifications. Train miners never to remove the SCSR mouthpiece to communicate during evacuation — use hand signals or written notes instead. Eliminate hot work near seals wherever an alternative method exists.

records.best_practice: Develop ground control plans that specify remedial measures for adverse conditions such as those presented by old underground mines. Do not work near dangerous highwalls or banks and be aware of changing highwall conditions. Train examiners to recognize adverse conditions and environmental factors that can decrease stability. Involve front line supervisors when developing mining plans and apply prudent engineering principles.

records.mine: Cayuga Mine / Cargill Deicing Technology (contr. Cayuga Crushed Stone WNK)
records.best_practice: Implement an annual structural inspection program for all surface bins, hoppers, and support structures, especially those exposed to corrosive materials. Follow up on engineering consultant recommendations within specified timelines. Measure shear tab thickness and connection integrity at scheduled intervals. Do not allow vehicles or personnel to position under bins without confirming structural integrity. Dismantle and replace severely corroded structures before returning to service.

records.mine: Upper Big Branch Mine-South / Performance Coal Company (Massey Energy)
records.equipment: Longwall shearer (bits y sprays) + polvo de carbón acumulado
records.best_practice: Maintain incombustible content (rock dust) at required levels throughout the mine — this is the last barrier that stops a local methane ignition from becoming a mine-wide coal dust explosion. Inspect shearer bits before every cut and replace worn or broken bits. Verify that every water spray on the shearer is clear and functioning. Provide ventilation sufficient to dilute and carry away methane at the face. Never maintain a second set of books or give advance warning of inspections — concealment does not remove hazards, it accumulates them. Protect miners who report safety concerns from retaliation.

records.best_practice: MSHA Fatal Alert CAI-2014-11: (1) Never operate articulated equipment with any body part outside the operator compartment — articulation points create fatal crush zones in seconds. (2) Immediately remove from service any piece of equipment with a defective steering control, even if the machine appears to function. Improvised repairs to safety-critical controls are not acceptable. (3) Pre-operational and weekly examinations must physically verify every safety-critical system: steering, brakes, emergency shutdowns. Paperwork showing "no defects" is not evidence of safety if the physical inspection was inadequate. (4) Mine management must establish written accountability mechanisms for equipment inspections, with follow-up verification that defects are actually found and corrected. (5) All articulated mobile equipment should be provided with an operator restraint system to prevent the body from entering articulation pinch points.

records.best_practice: Conduct a preshift examination of all areas where work is scheduled, including construction sites — if no preshift exam was done, no one may enter or work in that area. Never allow miners to work near overhanging rock brows without adequate vertical support (cable bolts, timber, or jacks). When a crack appears in a rib or brow, stop all work immediately and support the hazard before anyone re-enters the area. Four previous MSHA rib citations at the same mine were a clear warning that rib control was inadequate — take action before another miner is injured.

records.best_practice: Never use the Emergency Stop Override to tram a CMM during normal operations — the ESO must only be used to move a disabled machine for repair. Ensure the PDS is commissioned so that audible and visual warnings remain active when the ESO is engaged. Task train all CMM operators on PDS operation and ESO limitations before they operate the machine. Conduct dynamic PDS testing at the start of each shift. Mine management must enforce roof control plan Red Zone provisions and prohibit ESO misuse — if management is aware of a dangerous practice and does not stop it, they share responsibility for the outcome.

Comply with all previously issued MSHA safeguards regardless of when they were issued.

records.best_practice: Block all heavy components against motion before dismantling — never rely on gravity alone to keep a component in place during disassembly. Require a second person to be present when dismantling heavy components weighing over a specified threshold. Develop written step-by-step dismantling procedures for all major plant components, including specific blocking requirements at each step. Verify that trained miners are actually applying blocking procedures — training alone is not sufficient if practices are not monitored.

records.mine: Pleasant Hill Mine (ID U00104391B) / Carter Roag Coal Company, Randolph/Upshur County, WV — Mine ID corregido S417 via join Part50: 46-09027→46-08194 (operador Part50: Carter Roag Coal Company)
records.best_practice: Provide crossovers that are wide enough (minimum 48 inches), have adequate roof clearance (minimum 60 inches), and allow miners to safely climb over and descend from the conveyor belt. Install guards to prevent miners from crossing conveyor belts at locations where no adequate crossover is provided. Before placing a crossover in service, physically verify that a miner can safely use it with the belt running — test it yourself. Inspect crossovers periodically to confirm they are actually being used; thick undisturbed dust is a warning sign that the crossover is inadequate.

records.best_practice: When a crack appears in the rib during drilling, stop immediately and evaluate the full extent of the instability before proceeding. Never install a rib bolt by hand when the rib has a visible crack or when the bolt encounters unusual resistance — this signals the rib is actively failing. Train foremen that accepting multiple warnings from crew members and continuing the task is a critical failure of supervisory judgment.

records.best_practice: Recognize that removing adverse roof with a continuous mining machine creates an arched entry profile and angled rock brows that do not look like conventional rectangular or stair-stepped brows. Install supplemental support at angled brows, and avoid positioning yourself between a roof bolting machine and the rib where a brow overhangs.
